newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BORSODCHEM CLEARED OF ENVIRONMENT CHARGES.
newsitem.headline: BORSODCHEM CLEARED OF ENVIRONMENT CHARGES.

text.p: Hungarian chemicals company Borsodchem Rt said on Tuesday a court of appeal cleared it of illegal transport and disposal of hazardous waste for which it was earlier fined 20 million forints.
"The court of appeal found that the company's appeal was justified and reversed the first decision," Borsodchem said in a statement.
The company said that the court of appeal also established Borsodchem had not contravened regulations on hazardous waste transport and disposal, as said in the previous court decision.

Last November a waste disposal company, Styx, subcontractor for Borsodchem, MOL and Tiszai Power Plant, was fined 146 million forints for illegally dumping over 500 cubic metres of oil sludge, contaminated soil and other hazardous waste in at least 12 locations.
As a result, all major clients of Styx, including Borsodchem, were implicated in the case and convicted along with Styx.
"The supervision has established that Styx, as subcontractor, deposited Borsodchem's waste on Borsodchem territory, into officially approved waste disposal sites," Borsodchem said.
